scopeNote: Whole-internet scope per FORGE.md creative mandate. New batches must be category-diverse with at most 1 local/agency-adjacent idea. SHIPPED so far: ShipSafe, LeakCheck, ExposureCheck, DepCheck (the 'ship-safety suite' for vibe-coded apps — 4 tools that cross-promote; launch kit in marketing/suite-launch.md). The 5 parked ideas are the old narrow local set, kept for revival but off the active pick-list.

ideas.title: DepCheck — npm dependency risk scanner
ideas.oneliner: Paste your package.json and instantly see vulnerable, abandoned, typosquatted, and risky-licensed dependencies in plain English — only package names+versions are looked up, your code stays in the browser.
ideas.problem: Vibe coders and indie devs npm-install dozens of packages blind. They never check for known CVEs, abandoned packages, typosquats, copyleft licenses, or sketchy install scripts until something breaks or gets popped. The real tools (Snyk, Socket, npm audit) are dev-ops/CI heavy and non-experts don't run them.
ideas.who: Indie devs, no-code/vibe builders, students — the same audience as the rest of the ship-safety suite. Global.
ideas.gap: Vulnerability/supply-chain scanners are CI/dev-ops tools; there's no instant, plain-English, no-signup web tool that takes a pasted manifest and explains dependency risk to a non-expert. The wedge is framing + being the 4th tool in the suite.
ideas.buildPlan: Static page; parse package.json/lockfile, query the free CORS-enabled OSV.dev (vulns) + registry.npmjs.org (freshness/license) by name+version, plus offline typosquat (popular-list edit-distance) + hygiene checks. Reuses LeakCheck design. ~2-day build, zero-secret. Paid later: CI ruleset pack (shared with suite).
ideas.notes: SHIPPED 2026-06-08 — product #5, 4th tool in the ship-safety suite (ShipSafe/LeakCheck/ExposureCheck/DepCheck cross-link). Built by a 9-agent swarm (forked LeakCheck) that ALSO produced the suite launch kit in parallel. 0 blockers. Independently verified: only package name+version sent to OSV/npm (manifest body never leaves browser), XSS-safe (textContent), live test = 18 risks across 11 deps. Known limit: depends on OSV/npm registry (degrades to offline typosquat+hygiene). See builds/depcheck.md + marketing/suite-launch.md.

ideas.title: ExposureCheck — is your live site leaking?
ideas.oneliner: Enter your deployed URL (or paste your built bundle) and see what a public visitor can already grab: exposed .env/.git/config files, secrets hardcoded in your JS bundle, leaked source maps, and internal endpoints.
ideas.problem: Vibe-coded and rushed deploys routinely ship .env files, public .git folders, source maps, and hardcoded API keys to production where anyone can fetch them. Builders never check, and existing tools are dev-ops/pentest tools non-experts won't run.
ideas.who: Indie devs, no-code/vibe builders, and small teams who deployed fast — the same audience as the rest of the suite. Global.
ideas.gap: Server-side / pentest scanners exist but are technical; there's no instant, plain-English, no-signup web tool that checks a DEPLOYED site for leaked secrets/files/source and explains the fix. The wedge is framing + being the deployed-site sibling to LeakCheck.
ideas.buildPlan: Static page, client-side. URL mode fetches page + scripts via a public CORS-proxy chain and probes ~12 sensitive paths; paste mode (always works) analyzes a pasted bundle. Reuses LeakCheck detectors + design. ~2-3 day build, zero-secret.
ideas.notes: SHIPPED 2026-06-08 — product #4, ship-safety suite. Forked LeakCheck via a 7-agent swarm, 0 blockers. Verified: XSS-safe vs fetched content, secrets masked (16 exposures, no raw secret in DOM), defensive 'scan your own site' framing. Known limit: URL mode depends on public CORS proxies (paste mode is reliable). See builds/exposurecheck.md.

ideas.title: LeakCheck — paste-and-scan secret detector
ideas.oneliner: Paste a code snippet, .env, or config and instantly see exposed API keys, tokens, and private keys flagged by severity — 100% in your browser, nothing uploaded.
ideas.problem: Hardcoded secrets are the #1 way indie and AI-assisted projects get popped — keys committed to public repos, pasted into Discord, shipped in client bundles. Existing scanners (gitleaks, trufflehog) are CLI/dev-ops tools nobody outside security runs.
ideas.who: The whole developer internet, especially the explosion of vibe-coders / no-code builders, plus students and bootcamp grads.
ideas.gap: All credible scanners are CLI or CI-pipeline tools; there is no trustworthy, instant, plain-English web tool that runs entirely client-side (provably no upload) and explains WHICH secret, WHY it's dangerous, and HOW to rotate it.
ideas.buildPlan: Static page; regex/entropy ruleset runs in-browser with a 'nothing leaves this tab' guarantee. Severity-ranked findings + rotation steps. ~2-day build, zero-secret. Paid later: pre-commit ruleset / org policy pack.
ideas.notes: SHIPPED 2026-06-08 — product #3, FIRST under the widened-scope mandate, anchor of the suite's 'code secrets' leg. 7-agent swarm. Verified: zero network on user data, XSS-safe, secrets masked. Forked by ExposureCheck + DepCheck. See builds/leakcheck.md.

ideas.title: TrueRate — what to actually charge
ideas.oneliner: Enter your target take-home, real billable hours, expenses, and tax rate, and get the hourly/day rate you must charge to hit it — with every assumption shown.
ideas.problem: Freelancers chronically underprice because they price off a salary number and forget non-billable time, expenses, downtime, and self-employment tax.
ideas.who: The global freelance / contractor / solopreneur workforce.
ideas.gap: Most 'freelance rate calculators' are thin blog lead-magnets that gloss over tax and utilization. A transparent, shareable, does-the-math tool is underserved.
ideas.buildPlan: Static client-side calculator; inputs -> required rate with a labeled waterfall. Shareable URL. ~1-2 day build, zero-secret.
ideas.notes: Evergreen high-intent SEO. Owner found it weak in 2026-06-08 review; deprioritized in favor of the dev 'ship-safety' suite.

ideas.title: Caffeine Curve — see the coffee in your system
ideas.oneliner: Log your coffees and watch a live curve of caffeine in your bloodstream, plus when it'll drop below a sleep-safe level.
ideas.problem: People feel wired at 11pm and don't connect it to the 3pm latte. Caffeine has a ~5-6h half-life but nobody does that math.
ideas.who: Basically everyone who drinks caffeine and cares about sleep.
ideas.gap: No clean, instant, no-signup web tool plots YOUR intake as a live decay curve with a concrete 'safe to sleep by' time.
ideas.buildPlan: Static page; add drinks at times -> superposed decay curve + 'below 50mg by HH:MM'. Disclaimer, no medical advice. ~1-2 day build, zero-secret.
ideas.notes: Viral/shareable, strong evergreen SEO. Owner found it weak in 2026-06-08 review; deprioritized in favor of the dev suite.

ideas.title: SubAudit — your subscription reality check
ideas.oneliner: Add your subscriptions once and see your true annual spend, a renewal calendar you can export, and a ranked 'cancel these first' list by cost-per-use.
ideas.problem: Subscription creep is a near-universal money leak — people don't know their burn or when things renew.
ideas.who: Global consumers drowning in SaaS/streaming/app subscriptions.
ideas.gap: Automatic managers demand bank access most won't grant for a gut-check. A privacy-first, no-login, manual tool fills the trust gap.
ideas.buildPlan: Static page; localStorage list -> annualized total, per-use cost, renewal timeline, .ics export. ~2-day build, zero-secret.
ideas.notes: Privacy-first (no bank link) is the wedge AND the marketing angle. Strong SEO + a shareable 'I was paying $X/yr' moment.

ideas.title: DeckShare — flashcards in a link
ideas.oneliner: Make a flashcard deck in your browser, study it with spaced repetition, and share the whole deck as a single URL — no account, no app install.
ideas.problem: Anki is intimidating and install-heavy; Quizlet has paywalled study modes. Students just want to make a deck and send it in one click.
ideas.who: Students, language learners, and self-learners worldwide.
ideas.gap: The friction-free middle is open: free, no-login, genuinely-shareable deck with real spaced repetition and zero paywall.
ideas.buildPlan: Static SPA; SM-2 spaced repetition in localStorage, shareable deck URL or static publish. ~3-day build, zero-secret.
ideas.notes: Built-in word-of-mouth loop: every shared deck markets the tool. Public decks compound into an SEO content moat.

ideas.title: FrostPlan — when to plant, for your zip
ideas.oneliner: Enter your location and get your last/first frost dates plus a personalized seed-starting and planting calendar you can export as reminders.
ideas.problem: New gardeners kill plants by sowing too early. The frost-date + count-back math is annoying and scattered across extension PDFs.
ideas.who: The huge, global home-gardening hobby audience — spikes every spring.
ideas.gap: Frost-date lookups are ugly, ad-choked, and stop at the date. A clean personalized planting schedule with reminders is underserved.
ideas.buildPlan: Static page; bundled frost-date dataset + per-crop weeks table -> personalized calendar + .ics export. ~2-3 day build, zero-secret.
ideas.notes: Massive evergreen + seasonal SEO. Per-crop/per-region pages scale to thousands of long-tail landing pages.

ideas.title: RacePace — splits and goal times
ideas.oneliner: Enter a goal race time and get your exact per-mile/km splits, pace bands, and predicted finish times at every other distance.
ideas.problem: Runners need target splits and race-equivalency predictions but juggle spreadsheets or paywalled apps.
ideas.who: The global running and endurance community.
ideas.gap: Bare pace calculators exist, but few combine a clean split table + race-equivalency + a shareable race-day band in one polished tool.
ideas.buildPlan: Static calculator; goal time -> splits, pace bands, equivalent times. Printable race-day band. ~1-2 day build, zero-secret.
ideas.notes: Evergreen SEO. Printable pace band is a race-day virality hook. Win on polish + all-in-one.

ideas.title: PaletteForge — accessible color palettes
ideas.oneliner: Generate harmonious palettes and gradients, check every pair for WCAG contrast, and export straight to Tailwind, CSS variables, or SVG.
ideas.problem: Developers waste time hand-tuning palettes and ship inaccessible color combos. Existing generators rarely bake accessibility in or export to dev formats.
ideas.who: The global design + front-end developer community.
ideas.gap: Color tools are fragmented: generators ignore accessibility; checkers ignore generation; few export clean Tailwind/CSS tokens.
ideas.buildPlan: Static SPA; palette/gradient gen, live WCAG contrast grid, export to Tailwind/CSS vars/SVG/JSON. ~2-day build, zero-secret.
ideas.notes: Crowded space (Coolors etc.) — only ship if we win on accessibility-first + dev-export. Lowest-priority; included for breadth.

ideas.title: Vibe-Coded App Health Checker
ideas.oneliner: Paste a URL and get a plain-English report on ADA/WCAG gaps, missing privacy policy/cookie banner, broken schema, and demand-letter risk.
ideas.problem: AI tools produced an explosion of apps from non-devs who ship zero WCAG compliance (4,600+ ADA suits in 2024), no privacy policy, and broken ARIA — discovered only when a demand letter arrives.
ideas.who: Hundreds of thousands of indie / no-code builders shipping AI-generated sites.
ideas.gap: WAVE/axe/Lighthouse exist but NONE combine accessibility + privacy + schema + plain-English demand-letter framing in one non-technical report.
ideas.buildPlan: Serverless/proxy fetch wraps accessibility + privacy + schema checks. Plain-English risk report card. Paid tier: scheduled re-checks.
ideas.notes: Product #1, shipped. Anchor of the 'ship-safety suite' (legal/accessibility leg). Broad global dev audience.

ideas.title: ReserveRight (Winery & Charter edition)
ideas.oneliner: A drop-in deposit-and-hold widget that collects a Stripe deposit and sends reminder texts for wine tastings, tours, and fishing/kayak charters — no platform migration.
ideas.problem: No-shows destroy revenue on time-boxed experiences. Incumbents charge per-cover + monthly + a deposit fee or require full migration.
ideas.who: Sonoma's 425+ wineries and tasting rooms, fishing/kayak charters — Copper Bay's warm local channel.
ideas.gap: The generic restaurant deposit widget is already done well. Survives only as the winery/charter niche sold through Copper Bay's local relationships.
ideas.buildPlan: Static reserve page + Stripe Checkout deposit + Resend/Twilio reminders, embeddable as a <script>. 3-day Vercel build.
needsOwner: FORGE Stripe Connect platform account (white-label/reseller tier)
ideas.notes: PARKED 2026-06-08 under the widened-scope mandate: distribution depends entirely on the owner's private local channel. Revivable if the owner wants a local play.

ideas.title: Marina Slip Waitlist & Day-Use Lite
ideas.oneliner: A lightweight public waitlist plus day-use launch reservation page with deposit collection for small marinas and county boat launches.
ideas.problem: Most small marinas run on spreadsheets; the big suites are built for full-service marinas. County launches still mail PDF forms.
ideas.who: Sub-50-slip marinas, county park boat launches, yacht clubs, kayak/SUP outfitters.
ideas.gap: Snag-A-Slip is a marketplace; the big suites are over-built. Nothing affordable serves only waitlist + day-use for the smallest operators.
ideas.buildPlan: Calendar + form + Stripe deposit + Resend confirmation. 3-4 day Vercel build. Dog-food at Lake Sonoma Marina first.
ideas.notes: PARKED 2026-06-08 under widened scope. NOTE: most defensible of the parked set — complements the owner's existing marina-booking SaaS and has a real seed client (Lake Sonoma). Revive first if the owner wants a local one.

ideas.title: Job-Completion Report + Review Push
ideas.oneliner: Tech snaps before/after photos and the customer gets a branded PDF of what was done plus a one-tap Google-review CTA while the goodwill is fresh.
ideas.problem: CompanyCam is photo-only; the big suites bury photos inside expensive plans. Nobody owns the customer-facing 'completion moment'.
ideas.who: Roofers, painters, HVAC, plumbers — Copper Bay's trades base.
ideas.gap: Photo apps are internal-facing; suites treat photos as secondary; none close the customer-facing review loop with a branded completion report.
ideas.buildPlan: PWA camera + Cloudinary upload + client-side PDF + public report URL + Google-review deep link. 3-4 weeks.
ideas.notes: PARKED 2026-06-08 under widened scope (trades/local channel + heaviest build). Revivable as part of a Copper Bay trades stack.

ideas.title: Local GEO Audit (agency lead magnet)
ideas.oneliner: Enter a business name and location to get a report card on AI-Overview citation, LocalBusiness JSON-LD validity, and NAP consistency.
ideas.problem: AI Overviews hit ~25.8% of US searches and local businesses fear being invisible to AI search. Paid GEO tools are generalist and $49-199/mo.
ideas.who: Local businesses worried about AI-search visibility, and the agency that pitches them.
ideas.gap: Free AI-visibility checkers are already crowding; the zero-secret slice is an agency distribution asset, not a product.
ideas.buildPlan: Static explainer + client-side JSON-LD/schema validator + NAP check + 'book a GEO audit' CTA. 1-2 days.
needsOwner: SerpAPI/Serper (only for the live AI-Overview citation tier later)
ideas.notes: PARKED 2026-06-08: below threshold AND always an agency lead-magnet rather than a standalone product.

ideas.title: Review-Pulse (white-label add-on)
ideas.oneliner: A QR/link micro-app that routes happy customers to a Google review and unhappy ones to private feedback — sold as a configured, agency-branded add-on.
ideas.problem: Birdeye starts $299/mo and Podium $249-599 — priced for franchises, locking out solo operators.
ideas.who: Single-location local businesses already on Copper Bay's roster.
ideas.gap: The cheap standalone lane is saturated and the experience-gate pattern is a standard feature, not a differentiator.
ideas.buildPlan: Static page + Google Maps review deep-link + sentiment fork; no API keys for MVP. 1-2 days.
ideas.notes: PARKED 2026-06-08: below threshold and too crowded to win as a standalone. Only viable bundled into a Copper Bay trades stack.

ideas.title: Contractor Instant-Quote Page (agency-install)
ideas.oneliner: A done-for-you, pre-configured ballpark-estimate page for a trade vertical that qualifies inbound leads before the phone call.
ideas.problem: Trades waste ~15 min/call on tire-kickers. Field-service suites force the whole business onto a platform when the pain is one narrow page.
ideas.who: Plumbers, HVAC, landscapers, electricians, painters.
ideas.gap: Generic DIY quote-widget builders already exist and are free. The reshape to a consumer cost-estimator had no real distribution edge or moat.
ideas.buildPlan: JSON-driven question tree -> ballpark range -> lead email via Resend. 2-day build.
ideas.notes: KILLED by owner 2026-06-08. Teardown DONE — Pages disabled and repo archived/read-only (full hard-delete pending; PAT lacks delete_repo scope). No defensible distribution loop or moat. Do not revisit.

ideas.title: InvoiceQuick — ad-free invoice & quote generator
ideas.oneliner: Fill in your client and line items, pick a template, and get a clean PDF downloaded in 10 seconds — no signup, no ads, nothing leaves your browser.
ideas.problem: Every free invoice generator is plastered with ads and upsells, or forces a signup. Freelancers bounce between 3 ugly tools just to invoice a client.
ideas.who: Freelancers, independent contractors, and small creative agencies worldwide.
ideas.gap: 'Free invoice generator' is one of the highest-intent finance searches and every free incumbent monetizes through friction — no clean, ad-free, no-signup tool exists.
ideas.buildPlan: Static SPA; jsPDF renders invoice PDF entirely client-side — no server, no upload. Three bundled templates (minimal, classic, modern). Inputs: your details, client, line items, tax rate, due date, notes. localStorage saves last invoice as a draft. ~2-3 day build, zero-secret.
ideas.notes: 'Free invoice generator' is among the top finance search queries globally. Key differentiation: zero ads, no signup, polished templates, offline-capable. Template library grows into a mild content moat. Paid tier: premium template packs ($4.99 one-time). Reddit r/freelance confirms recurring complaint about ad-choked incumbents.

ideas.title: DebtViz — animated debt payoff comparison
ideas.oneliner: Enter your debts and see avalanche vs. snowball racing to zero as a live animated chart — with exact interest saved and months difference — then share your scenario.
ideas.problem: People endlessly debate avalanche vs. snowball but no tool shows both strategies side-by-side as an animation so the tradeoff clicks emotionally, not just mathematically.
ideas.who: Adults with consumer debt globally — the 25M+ r/personalfinance audience is the beachhead.
ideas.gap: Static debt calculators and tables exist everywhere; a genuinely animated, shareable, side-by-side comparison tool does not.
ideas.buildPlan: Static page; Chart.js animated bar chart. Input: debt list (name, balance, APR, minimum payment) + extra monthly payment. Computes both strategies month-by-month, animates payoff race, shows interest-total delta and timeline. Shareable URL encodes the full debt scenario. ~2-day build, zero-secret.
ideas.notes: Animated visual is the clear differentiator vs. static incumbents (Undebt.it, Credit Karma). Shareable debt scenario URL is the word-of-mouth engine. r/personalfinance is a natural distribution channel — these posts routinely go viral. 'Avalanche vs snowball calculator' is a high-intent evergreen query.

ideas.title: BurnoutIndex — burnout self-assessment with trend tracking
ideas.oneliner: A 16-question burnout check that scores you across exhaustion, cynicism, and efficacy — then tracks your score over time in your browser so you can see burnout building before it hits.
ideas.problem: Burnout sneaks up gradually; one-off quizzes tell you where you are today but nothing tracks the drift. Clinical tools are PDFs; wellness quizzes are single-use fluff with no follow-up.
ideas.who: Knowledge workers, remote workers, and managers globally — anyone tracking their mental health.
ideas.gap: No clean, no-login web tool combines a validated burnout assessment with longitudinal trend tracking and a shareable result card.
ideas.buildPlan: Static page; 16-question Maslach-inspired assessment scoring 3 dimensions. Radar chart of results. localStorage stores each check-in with timestamp; sparkline shows trend across sessions. 'My burnout score this week' shareable image card. ~2-day build, zero-secret. Disclaimer: informational only, not a clinical diagnostic.
ideas.notes: Trend tracking is the wedge — one-time burnout quizzes are everywhere; none show you deteriorating over 4 weeks, which is what prompts action. 'Burnout test' = 50K+ monthly searches. Shareable score card drives word-of-mouth in Slack/LinkedIn. Must include clear disclaimer.

ideas.title: MeetingMeter — live meeting cost clock
ideas.oneliner: Set attendee count and average salary, press Start, and watch the dollar cost tick up in real time — then screenshot it and post it.
ideas.problem: Meetings are expensive and invisible. Nobody feels the $3,000/hour price tag of a 10-person leadership sync until they see the ticker running.
ideas.who: Tech workers, managers, and anyone who has ever sat through a pointless meeting — a universally relatable global audience.
ideas.gap: Static meeting cost calculators exist but no live, dramatic ticker with a shareable screenshot moment — that UX doesn't exist.
ideas.buildPlan: Static page; JS setInterval × (attendees × hourly rate / 3600) ticks every 100ms. Live animated counter. Currency selector. 'Copy screenshot' button captures current reading as a canvas image. Salary presets (junior dev team, senior team, exec meeting). ~1-2 day build, zero-secret.
ideas.notes: Viral on LinkedIn/Twitter among tech workers — 'this meeting cost $842' screenshot is a natural post. Very fast build (potentially 1-day ship). Fastest time-to-live of any idea in this batch. HN May 2026 'what do you still do manually' thread confirms recurring meeting-friction pain.

ideas.title: VerbDrill — language verb conjugation trainer
ideas.oneliner: Drill verb conjugations for Spanish, French, German, Italian, or Portuguese with real spaced repetition — in your browser, no account, no app install.
ideas.problem: Verb conjugation is the hardest wall in language learning. Duolingo buries drills in gamification; dedicated conjugation sites are clunky, ad-heavy, or mobile-only.
ideas.who: Language learners globally — Spanish alone has 100M+ active learners; French and German add tens of millions more.
ideas.gap: A clean, no-login, browser-native conjugation driller with genuine spaced repetition and multi-language coverage in one tool doesn't exist.
ideas.buildPlan: Static SPA; bundled JSON dataset: top 100 verbs × 5 languages × major tenses (present, preterite, imperfect, future, conditional, subjunctive). Drill: show English infinitive, user types conjugated form, SM-2 scoring tracked in localStorage. Streak counter. ~3-day build, zero-secret (all data bundled).
ideas.notes: Language learning is one of the largest self-improvement categories online. Long-tail SEO: per-language and per-tense landing pages compound (e.g. 'practice Spanish subjunctive online') into a large organic surface. Verb dataset + individual spaced-repetition progress is a mild defensibility moat. Distinct from DeckShare (content-first with curated data, not a user-created flashcard platform).

ideas.title: PostSize — multi-platform social media image resizer
ideas.oneliner: Drop an image, select your platforms (Instagram, LinkedIn, Twitter/X, TikTok, YouTube), and download all correctly-sized crops at once — no signup, no watermark.
ideas.problem: Content creators waste time bouncing between single-platform resizers every time they post, because every social network has different aspect ratios and pixel requirements.
ideas.who: Content creators, freelance social media managers, and small business owners worldwide.
ideas.gap: Canva's bulk export requires a paid subscription; all free resizers handle only one platform at a time — a no-signup, all-platforms-at-once tool doesn't exist.
ideas.buildPlan: Static page; HTML5 Canvas API processes and crops image client-side. 18+ platform dimension presets with labels. Side-by-side crop previews. Download all as ZIP (JSZip) or individually. ~2-3 day build, zero-secret.
ideas.notes: Platform-specific queries ('instagram post size 2026', 'linkedin banner dimensions', 'youtube thumbnail size') generate constant high-intent search traffic. Download-all-at-once is the clear differentiator. Canvas API crop math makes this a slightly heavier build than average.

ideas.title: TechTimeline — your life mapped to tech history
ideas.oneliner: Enter your birth year and get a personalized timeline of the internet and tech milestones that shaped your life — then share it as a card.
ideas.problem: People love contextualizing their life against history, but generic 'what happened the year I was born' tools are dull. A tech-specific lens is instantly shareable by the internet-native generation.
ideas.who: Anyone born between 1960-2010 who has ever thought 'wait, how old was I when the iPhone came out?' — a multi-billion-person audience.
ideas.gap: History-in-context tools are generic; no clean, shareable, tech-milestones-specific timeline generator exists.
ideas.buildPlan: Static page; bundled JSON dataset of ~150 curated tech milestones (1950-2025). User enters birth year → milestones rendered as a personalized timeline with relative ages ('You were 6 when Google launched'). HTML5 Canvas renders a shareable card image. ~2-day build, zero-secret.
ideas.notes: Pure viral mechanic: personalized + shareable = natural tweet/post fodder for the tech community. Dataset is static and bundled — zero maintenance. Low direct monetization but strong for portfolio visibility and audience building. Evergreen — dataset grows 1 entry per year.

ideas.title: FastClock — intermittent fasting timer & streak tracker
ideas.oneliner: Set your eating window, see exactly how many hours you've been fasting and when your next window opens — plus a daily streak you can share.
ideas.problem: Intermittent fasting apps (Zero, Life Fasting) are mobile-only, require downloads, and push subscriptions. There's no clean, instant, no-account web timer for tracking your fast.
ideas.who: The 10M+ intermittent fasting community and any health-conscious person tracking their eating window.
ideas.gap: Mobile apps dominate IF tracking; the web-based equivalent — no download, no account, use it right now — is a clear and unoccupied gap.
ideas.buildPlan: Static page; user sets eating window times (e.g. 12pm-8pm). Live timer shows fasting/eating status, hours fasted so far, countdown to next window. Animated circular progress ring. localStorage persists eating window + daily streak. Shareable streak card. Disclaimer: not medical advice. ~2-day build, zero-secret.
ideas.notes: r/intermittentfasting has 500K+ members; Zero app has 10M+ downloads — proven demand, web gap confirmed. SEO: 'intermittent fasting timer online', '16:8 fasting timer web'. Streak card is the shareable hook. Disclaimer required.
